summary: Ayers Rock Connellan Airport (AYQ) is the sole gateway to Uluru-Kata Tjuta National Park, serving the remote township of Yulara in Australia's Northern Territory. The airport was named after Eddie Connellan, a pioneering outback aviator who established air links across Central Australia in the 1930s. Its isolated desert location, roughly 20 km from the Uluru monolith, makes it one of Australia's most tourism-dependent airports despite handling modest passenger volumes.
faqs:
Q: How far is Ayers Rock Airport from Uluru?
A: The airport is approximately 20 km (12 miles) from Uluru, with a driving time of about 25 minutes to the rock itself and the Yulara township.

Q: Which airlines operate from Ayers Rock Connellan Airport?
A: Qantas and QantasLink provide scheduled jet and turboprop services from destinations such as Sydney, Melbourne, Cairns, and Alice Springs. Charter flights also operate seasonally.

Q: Does the airport have its own terminal facilities?
A: Yes, the airport has a single compact terminal with basic amenities including a cafe, souvenir shop, and car rental desks, reflecting its tourism-focused operations.

Q: Why was the town of Yulara built near the airport?
A: Yulara was developed in the 1970s-80s to consolidate tourism accommodation away from Uluru, and the airport was relocated nearby to support this purpose-built resort town.
transport_tips: Free shuttle buses connect the airport with all major Yulara resorts and the Ayers Rock Resort campground, typically timed to meet each flight. Rental cars are available from major agencies at the terminal and are useful for visiting Uluru and Kata Tjuta at your own pace, though note that the parks require a separate entry permit. There is no public bus service in the region, so pre-arranged transfers or shuttle bookings are essential.
local_tip: Book sunrise flights when possible — arriving early in the morning via the eastern approach often gives passengers a stunning aerial view of Uluru and Kata Tjuta lit by the dawn light, something many travellers miss when flying in midday.
